description: Pollo alla Cacciatora, or Hunter Style Chicken, is a rustic and deeply flavorful Italian dish featuring tender chicken braised in a rich tomato sauce with bell peppers, onions, and often mushrooms. This comforting classic embodies the heart of Italian home cooking, perfect for a satisfying family meal. Its robust flavors are a testament to simple, quality ingredients cooked with care.

instructions.title: Prepare and Brown the Chicken
instructions.text: Pat the chicken pieces dry with paper towels and season generously with salt and black pepper. Heat 2 tablespoons of olive oil in a large Dutch oven or heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat. Sear the chicken in batches, skin-side down first, until golden brown and crisp, about 5-7 minutes per side. Remove chicken from the pot and set aside.

instructions.title: Sauté Aromatics and Vegetables
instructions.text: Reduce the heat to medium. Add the remaining 1 tablespoon of olive oil to the pot. Add the chopped onion and cook until softened, about 3-4 minutes. Stir in the minced garlic and cook for another minute until fragrant. Add the sliced red and green bell peppers and mushrooms, cooking for 5-7 minutes until they begin to soften.

instructions.title: Deglaze with White Wine
instructions.text: Pour in the dry white wine, scraping the bottom of the pot with a wooden spoon to loosen any browned bits. Let the wine simmer and reduce by half, which should take about 2-3 minutes. This step adds depth of flavor to the sauce.

instructions.title: Add Tomatoes and Herbs
instructions.text: Stir in the crushed tomatoes and chicken broth. Add the fresh rosemary sprigs, thyme sprigs, and bay leaf. Bring the sauce to a gentle simmer, stirring occasionally.

instructions.title: Simmer the Chicken
instructions.text: Return the browned chicken pieces to the pot, nestling them into the sauce. Ensure the chicken is partially submerged. Reduce the heat to low, cover the pot, and let it simmer for 25-30 minutes, or until the chicken is cooked through and tender, reaching an internal temperature of 165F (74C).

instructions.title: Final Touches and Serve
instructions.text: Remove the herb sprigs and bay leaf from the pot. Taste the sauce and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper as needed. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley. Serve hot, directly from the pot or transferred to a serving platter, with your favorite side dishes.

tips: For richer flavor, use good quality San Marzano tomatoes. Their natural sweetness and lower acidity enhance the sauce significantly.
Do not overcrowd the pot when browning the chicken; work in batches to ensure a good sear, which locks in flavor and creates a crisp skin.
This dish tastes even better the next day as the flavors meld. Reheat gently on the stovetop or in the oven, adding a splash of broth if needed.
article:
Discover the heartwarming essence of Italian home cooking with Pollo alla Cacciatora, affectionately known as Hunter Style Chicken. This rustic, flavorful dish is a testament to the simplicity and richness of Italian cuisine, transforming humble ingredients into a truly memorable meal. Imagine tender chicken pieces, slow-cooked in a savory sauce brimming with ripe tomatoes, aromatic herbs, and earthy vegetables – a symphony of flavors that evokes the rolling hills and sun-drenched kitchens of Italy.

Pollo alla Cacciatora isn't just a recipe; it's a culinary journey, a dish steeped in tradition and regional variations. Whether you're a seasoned chef or a home cook eager to explore Italian classics, mastering this recipe will bring a taste of authentic Italy right to your dining table. Get ready to impress your family and friends with a dish that's both comforting and elegant, a true celebration of Italian flavors.

## What is Chicken Cacciatore?

The name "Cacciatore" literally means "hunter" in Italian, giving us "hunter-style chicken." The dish originated as a practical meal prepared by hunters in the field, utilizing readily available ingredients such as wild game, mushrooms, onions, and herbs. Over time, chicken became the more common protein, and the recipe evolved into the beloved classic we know today.

At its heart, Pollo alla Cacciatora is a braised chicken dish. Chicken pieces, often bone-in and skin-on for maximum flavor, are seared until golden, then slow-cooked in a rich, rustic sauce. While the core components – chicken, tomatoes, onions, garlic, and bell peppers – remain consistent, regional variations abound. Some recipes call for red wine, others white; some include mushrooms and olives, while others focus purely on the tomato and pepper base. Northern Italian versions might lean towards mushrooms and white wine, while southern interpretations often feature red wine, tomatoes, and sometimes a hint of spice. Regardless of the nuances, the result is always a deeply flavorful, tender chicken dish with a sauce perfect for soaking up with crusty bread or serving over pasta. This traditional **Chicken Cacciatore** is a staple in Italian homes for good reason.

## Ingredients You Need for Pollo alla Cacciatora

Crafting the perfect Pollo alla Cacciatora begins with selecting fresh, high-quality ingredients. Here’s what you’ll need to gather:

*   **Chicken:** 8 pieces of bone-in, skin-on chicken (a mix of thighs, drumsticks, and breasts works well). Bone-in chicken adds depth of flavor and keeps the meat moist during slow cooking.
*   **Olive Oil:** 2-3 tablespoons of good quality extra virgin olive oil for searing and sautéing.
*   **Onion:** 1 large yellow onion, diced, forming the aromatic base.
*   **Garlic:** 4-6 cloves, minced, for that unmistakable Italian flavor.
*   **Bell Peppers:** 1 red and 1 yellow bell pepper, deseeded and sliced into strips, adding sweetness and color.
*   **Mushrooms (Optional):** 8 ounces cremini or button mushrooms, sliced, for an earthy umami note.
*   **Tomato Paste:** 2 tablespoons, for intensifying the tomato flavor and enriching the sauce.
*   **Dry Red Wine:** 1 cup (e.g., Chianti, Merlot, or Cabernet Sauvignon) for deglazing and adding complexity. If you prefer to omit alcohol, use chicken broth.
*   **Canned Tomatoes:** 28 ounces crushed San Marzano tomatoes (or good quality diced tomatoes). San Marzano tomatoes are prized for their balanced sweetness and low acidity.
*   **Chicken Broth:** 1/2 cup, if needed to thin the sauce or if not using wine.
*   **Fresh Herbs:** 2 sprigs fresh rosemary, 3-4 sprigs fresh thyme, and 1 teaspoon dried oregano. Fresh herbs make a significant difference.
*   **Salt and Black Pepper:** To taste, for seasoning the chicken and the sauce.
*   **Olives (Optional):** 1/2 cup Kalamata or black olives, pitted, for a briny counterpoint.
*   **Fresh Parsley:** For garnish, chopped.

## Step-by-Step Instructions for Hunter Style Chicken

Making Pollo alla Cacciatora is a rewarding experience. Follow these steps for a delicious result:

1.  **Prepare the Chicken:** Pat the chicken pieces thoroughly dry with paper towels. Season generously all over with salt and freshly ground black pepper. This step is crucial for crispy skin and flavorful meat.
2.  **Sear the Chicken:** Heat the olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Once shimmering, add the chicken pieces skin-side down, in batches if necessary, to avoid overcrowding. Sear for 5-7 minutes per side until the skin is golden brown and crispy. Remove the chicken from the pot and set aside on a plate.
3.  **Sauté Aromatics and Vegetables:** Reduce the heat to medium. Add the diced onion to the pot and cook, stirring occasionally, until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Add the minced garlic and sliced bell peppers (and mushrooms, if using) and cook for another 5-7 minutes until the vegetables are slightly softened.
4.  **Build the Sauce Base:** Stir in the tomato paste and cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly, to deepen its flavor.
5.  **Deglaze with Wine:** Pour in the red wine (or chicken broth if omitting wine) and scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot with a wooden spoon. Bring to a simmer and let it cook for 2-3 minutes to allow the alcohol to evaporate slightly.
6.  **Add Tomatoes and Herbs:** Stir in the crushed San Marzano tomatoes, fresh rosemary sprigs, fresh thyme sprigs, and dried oregano. Bring the sauce to a gentle simmer.
7.  **Braise the Chicken:** Carefully return the seared chicken pieces to the pot, nestling them into the sauce. Add the pitted olives now if you are using them. Ensure the chicken is mostly submerged in the sauce.
8.  **Slow Cook:** Reduce the heat to low, cover the pot, and simmer gently for 45 minutes to 1 hour, or until the chicken is fork-tender and cooked through. Alternatively, you can braise it in a preheated oven at 350°F (175°C) for the same duration. The slow cooking allows the flavors to meld beautifully and the chicken to become incredibly tender.
9.  **Finish and Serve:** Remove the rosemary and thyme sprigs. Taste the sauce and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper as needed. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley before serving.

## Pro Tips for the Best Chicken Cacciatore

Achieving an exceptional Pollo alla Cacciatora involves a few key techniques:

*   **Dry Chicken is Key:** Always pat your chicken dry before searing. Moisture inhibits browning, and that golden, crispy skin adds a crucial layer of flavor to the dish.
*   **Don't Overcrowd the Pan:** Searing chicken in batches ensures proper browning. If the pan is too full, the chicken will steam instead of sear, resulting in pale, less flavorful skin.
*   **Quality Tomatoes Matter:** San Marzano tomatoes are often considered the gold standard for Italian sauces due to their balanced sweetness and low acidity. Using high-quality canned tomatoes will significantly elevate your sauce.
*   **Deglaze Thoroughly:** After searing the chicken and sautéing the vegetables, deglazing the pot with wine or broth helps release all the flavorful browned bits stuck to the bottom, incorporating them into your sauce.
*   **Low and Slow Braise:** The magic of **Chicken Cacciatore** happens during the long, gentle simmer. This slow cooking process tenderizes the chicken and allows the complex flavors of the sauce to fully develop and meld.
*   **Fresh Herbs for Fresh Flavor:** While dried herbs are convenient, fresh rosemary and thyme bring a vibrant, aromatic quality that truly enhances the dish.
*   **Taste and Adjust:** Always taste your sauce before serving. Adjust salt, pepper, or even a pinch of sugar if your tomatoes are a bit acidic, to achieve a perfectly balanced flavor profile.
*   **Resting Time:** Like many braised dishes, Pollo alla Cacciatora benefits from a short rest (5-10 minutes) off the heat before serving, allowing the flavors to settle and the chicken to reabsorb its juices.

## Serving Suggestions for Pollo alla Cacciatora

Pollo alla Cacciatora is a hearty and satisfying meal on its own, but its rich sauce begs for accompaniments that can soak up every last drop.

*   **Pasta:** Serve it over wide, flat pasta like tagliatelle or pappardelle, allowing the noodles to be generously coated in the savory sauce. Even simple spaghetti or penne works wonderfully.
*   **Polenta:** Creamy polenta is a classic pairing, offering a comforting base that perfectly complements the rustic chicken and sauce.
*   **Crusty Bread:** A warm, crusty loaf of Italian bread or baguette is essential for dipping into the flavorful sauce – a truly delightful experience.
*   **Rice:** Steamed white rice or a light pilaf can also serve as a neutral canvas for the rich flavors of the cacciatore.
*   **Roasted Potatoes:** Simple roasted potatoes or mashed potatoes provide a comforting side that pairs well with the tender chicken.
*   **Green Salad:** A light, refreshing green salad with a simple vinaigrette can cut through the richness of the dish, offering a pleasant contrast.
*   **Wine Pairing:** A medium-bodied red wine, such as Chianti, Sangiovese, or Merlot, will beautifully complement the robust flavors of this Italian classic.

## Variations and Substitutions

While the classic Pollo alla Cacciatora recipe is fantastic, it's also incredibly versatile, allowing for various adaptations based on preference or availability.

*   **Meat Alternatives:** While chicken is traditional, this "hunter-style" preparation can be applied to other meats. Rabbit cacciatore is a popular choice, and you could even experiment with pork shoulder or firm white fish, adjusting cooking times accordingly.
*   **Vegetable Additions:** Feel free to bulk up the vegetable content. Carrots, celery, zucchini, or even artichoke hearts can be added along with the bell peppers for extra flavor and nutrients.
*   **Wine Alternatives:** If you prefer not to use red wine, white wine (such as Pinot Grigio or Sauvignon Blanc) can be used for a slightly lighter sauce. For an alcohol-free version, simply use extra chicken broth.
*   **Spicy Kick:** For those who enjoy a bit of heat, a pinch of red pepper flakes added with the garlic and onions will give the sauce a delightful zing.
*   **Olives and Capers:** While optional in our main recipe, Kalamata or black olives and capers add a briny, tangy depth that many find essential to their perfect **Chicken Cacciatore**.
*   **Herb Variations:** Experiment with other fresh herbs like bay leaf or fresh sage for different aromatic profiles.
*   **Slow Cooker/Instant Pot:** This dish adapts beautifully to modern cooking methods. For a slow cooker, sear the chicken and sauté the aromatics on the stovetop, then combine everything in the slow cooker and cook on low for 4-6 hours. For an Instant Pot, use the sauté function for searing and sautéing, then pressure cook for 15-20 minutes with a natural release.

Pollo alla Cacciatora is more than just a meal; it's an experience. Its rustic charm and deep, comforting flavors make it a perfect dish for family dinners, special occasions, or simply a cozy night in. By following these steps and incorporating our pro tips, you'll create an authentic Italian masterpiece that transports you straight to the heart of Italy with every delicious bite. Enjoy the process, savor the aromas, and delight in the rich taste of your homemade Hunter Style Chicken.
